[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L5 verapamil gut-wall records show high jejunal and Caco-2 permeability (jejunal Peff ~1e-4 cm/s; Caco-2 Papp 25.2e-6 cm/s and concentration-dependent increases up to ~157e-6 cm/s), passive-diffusion-dominated transport, and only a minor role for P-gp efflux; intestinal CYP3A4 activity did not reduce verapamil permeability.

L5 also documents intestinal first-pass metabolism of verapamil (saturable norverapamil formation in rat intestinal mucosa), but the direct human fasted absolute F anchor for verapamil is 22% (17-29%), above the 20% threshold despite this first-pass loss.

The query shares the verapamil 3,4-dimethoxyphenethyl-methylamino-propyl chain and basic tertiary amine for which L4/L5 records demonstrate complete human intestinal absorption (Fa 95-100%) and high permeability; the lactam replacement provides no affirmative evidence of poor absorption or overwhelming efflux.

The only sub-20% direct anchors are non-gold L2 gallopamil values (15-23%) and a rabbit ketotifen value (8%); they conflict with the gallopamil L1 gold (96.3%) or are species-mismatched, so they do not affirmatively support F<20% for the query.
Other L1 gold anchors for structurally related molecules (drotaverine 58.2±18.2%, bevantolol 57%, vernakalant 58-71%, ketotifen >50%, NNC high) are all above 20%, supporting the high class.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the exact query molecule.
The benzazepinone lactam's effect on first-pass metabolism and efflux is not directly measured; verapamil gut-wall data may not fully transfer.
Verapamil fasted F range (17-29%) includes values below 20%, so the closest anchor is borderline.
Gallopamil L1 gold (96.3%) conflicts with L2 values (15-23%), leaving uncertainty in the closest acyclic analog.
No human intestinal metabolism or efflux data exist for the query itself.
Solubility and dissolution for the query are not experimentally measured.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) with moderate confidence. L5 verapamil gut-wall records confirm high passive permeability and minor P-gp efflux, with intestinal CYP3A4 not limiting permeability; the main first-pass loss is metabolism, yet the most transferable direct human F anchor (verapamil fasted 22%, 17-29%) remains above threshold. The query's verapamil-like chain supports adequate absorption, and no affirmative low-F evidence applies. Confidence stays moderate because no direct F exists for the exact query and the lactam's first-pass behavior is unknown.
